statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in the current hour and Tail is held at the closed-venue floor of 5%. Stress is unchanged at 54%: another hour without a verified kinetic step in the US-Iran tanker exchange is offset by Iran’s military threatening more severe strikes on US naval forces and by an Israeli assessment that Tehran is seeking a coordinated regional assault, neither of which has met an equity quote. The scheduled 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this horizon.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant weekend hours and rises gradually to 13% in the final hour of the halt, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green for the first 21 published hours. The 22:00 UTC reopening hour and the first full hour after it are each scored at 20% Tail and therefore map to WATCH and yellow; together they form the only published danger window. The final slot steps back to 17% and green on the assumption of an orderly two-way auction. Stress runs from 54% down to a 52% low and then rebuilds to 70% at the reopen, entering the high band in the last five slots. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% as later slots rest on progressively older evidence.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 into the final day of the CME weekend halt as the Hormuz exchange stays two-sided and unconfirmed; the 22:00 UTC reopen and the hour after it are the horizon’s two WATCH slots
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this forecast, and the horizon now also contains the second hour of the new session.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 56,000 expected, with July revised to a 21,000 gain and the unemployment rate steady at 4.1%. The 2-year yield rose about 5 basis points to 4.38%, its highest since January 2025, and the 10-year added a basis point to 4.776%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 3 September carries 4.34% and 4.77% for those maturities, consistent with that move. Rate futures shifted to price roughly a 59% probability of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC. Equities absorbed the repricing calmly: the Nasdaq-100 held a small gain and VIX closed at 14.53 against a 14.32 previous close. A separate unresolved strand is the trade-embargo threat made late in Friday’s session, which tied possible embargoes on deficit partners to a demand for lower policy rates.

The geopolitical sequence has not advanced kinetically in roughly eleven hours, but the rhetorical perimeter widened overnight. US Central Command says American forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers on Saturday morning after an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer were targeted by ballistic missiles; two vessels were permanently disabled and a third, unladen, was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman, and Adm. Brad Cooper said the US would destroy Iran’s oil fleet if necessary. Iran’s military then threatened that strikes would be "more severe than before" if harassment of Iranian shipping continues, and the IRGC claimed it had targeted three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels elsewhere; CENTCOM says neither US ship was hit and the IRGC counter-claim remains unconfirmed. Israeli reporting adds an assessment that Tehran is working to coordinate Hezbollah, Hamas and Houthi forces for a simultaneous assault, which is an intelligence assessment rather than a verified action. The campaign therefore remains two-sided and unresolved rather than a confirmed escalation ladder, which is why Stress carries it and Tail does not.

Cross-asset context remains conflicted rather than aligned. WTI is quoted near $91.5 after a weekly gain of roughly 9% and a monthly gain above 21%, an oil-led risk premium that pulls against equities. Friday’s internals were rotational: every tracked semiconductor name rose, led by Micron and AMD, while five of eight megacaps fell, including Tesla, Apple and Microsoft, and delayed index futures closed split with NQ up 0.14% against ES down 0.42% and YM down 0.57%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and belong in Stress, not in Tail.

The structural feature of this horizon is that roughly 49 hours of accumulated and so far unpriced information, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint, an energy premium and untested hawkish rate pricing all meet a single opening auction rather than a continuous session. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so cash equities are closed and the futures session that follows the reopen is a shortened holiday session with a midday halt, which implies thinner liquidity around any gap. That concentration is scored as a 20% Tail allowance in the 22:00 and 23:00 UTC slots, which maps to WATCH and yellow and forms the only published danger window, then steps down to 17% in the following hour. It is a conditional gap-and-extension allowance, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of this sequence. Every earlier hour remains at the closed-venue floor and maps to EA_ON. The next seven-day calendar is led by PPI on Thursday 10 September and CPI on Friday 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, with the 15-16 September FOMC beyond this window.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 01:00 UTC on 5 September to 00:00 UTC on 6 September and lie entirely inside the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from 01:00 UTC through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the Iranian counter-claim was published, then eased through 56% and 55% to 54% in the final slot as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout, reflecting a complete evidence set in which only the live price path was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Twenty-one of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail on a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, lifting from 06:00 UTC as the Tel Aviv and Gulf Sunday cash sessions provide the first equity quotes since Friday and reaching 13% in the last full hour of the halt as a pre-auction gap allowance. The final three slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. The reopening hour and the first full hour after it each carry a 20% Tail allowance, map to WATCH and yellow, and together form the only published danger window; the last slot steps back to 17% and green. Stress opens at 54%, reaches a 52% low in the quietest overnight hours, rebuilds through the Sunday sessions and reaches 70% at the reopen, entering the high band in the final five slots. The drivers are a two-sided and unconfirmed Hormuz tanker campaign now accompanied by an explicit Iranian threat of more severe strikes, an oil complex up roughly 9% on the week, hawkish September rate pricing after the 162K August payroll print, and an unresolved trade-embargo threat, none of which has met an equity quote since Friday. The Labor Day holiday calendar implies thinner liquidity around the reopen. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. Orderly two-way retracement at the reopen would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.
